blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-accessibility-1 (Field errors are conveyed by a red border only, with no text) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
`field--invalid`, a red border (`#e5484d`); the list of errors at the top of
the page is removed, since the red border already shows where the problem
is. No message text is added, to keep the form compact.
findings.recommendation: A screen reader user who leaves the postcode field with `ABC` hears nothing: the border colour is not exposed to assistive technology, and the only text that named the error ("Enter a 5-digit postcode, such as 75011.", from rules.ts) is the summary list the design removes. A colour-blind user cannot tell the red border from the grey one. Neither can learn which field is wrong or how to fix it, so the checkout cannot be completed (WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color, 3.3.1 Error Identification, 3.3.3 Error Suggestion, 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value). Show the message rules.ts already returns as text under each invalid field, tie it to the input with `aria-describedby`, and set `aria-invalid="true"` on the input while it is invalid; keep the red border as an addition. Update the spec's scenarios ("THEN the field's border turns red") to require the message and its association, and task 1.2 to test them.
findings.title: Field errors are conveyed by a red border only, with no text

findings.evidence:
the list of errors at the top of
the page is removed
findings.recommendation: Today the summary is rendered with `role="alert"` (Form.tsx:22), so pressing Pay with invalid fields is announced. The design removes it and says nothing of what happens on submit: a keyboard or screen reader user who never left a field, or who skipped past one, presses Pay and nothing happens and nothing is announced, with focus left on the button (WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification, 4.1.3 Status Messages, 2.4.3 Focus Order). State the submit behaviour in the design and the spec: on a failed submit, validate every field, show each inline message, and move focus to the first invalid field (or keep an error summary with links to the fields), with a scenario for it.
findings.title: A failed submit is no longer announced and focus is not moved
